note: Chapter 3 from docs/chapter-03/CHAPTER_03_PRODUCTION.md. Human lines are overheard; humans can't see or hear the spirits.

C3_00_barge.speaker: narrator
C3_00_barge.text: A flat barge stacked with paper bales is pushing off from the pier. It's bound downriver, for Bandar Kencana.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: The duo ride on top of the paper all morning. Reno counts herons. Lumi counts Reno's herons and corrects him.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: We can catch it tomorrow. It goes every morning.

bk01_barge_home.speaker: narrator
bk01_barge_home.text: The paper barge goes back upriver to Senja River Landing.

C3_01_wharf.speaker: narrator
C3_01_wharf.text: Bandar Kencana: printing shops, paper merchants and the smell of fresh ink.

C3_01_wharf.speaker: printer
C3_01_wharf.text: (to the trader) Proofs for the... for the Bandar... what's this town called again?

C3_01_wharf.speaker: trader
C3_01_wharf.text: Ha! Long week. It's Bandar... um.

C3_01_wharf.speaker: reno
C3_01_wharf.text: They forgot the name of their own town?

C3_01_wharf.speaker: lumi
C3_01_wharf.text: Reno. Smell that. It's the same ink as Nenek Arus's pool.

C3_01_wharf.speaker: narrator
C3_01_wharf.text: Somewhere along the shophouses, a radio crackles. "...anybody... valve... ANYBODY..."

C3_01_wharf.speaker: narrator
C3_01_wharf.text: New goal: find out what's crackling in the radio shop.

human_printer.speaker: printer
human_printer.text: (muttering over a proof sheet) The masthead's blank. I set those letters myself. Bandar... Ken... no.

human_trader.speaker: trader
human_trader.text: (to nobody) Thirty years selling paper in... this town. It's on the tip of my tongue.

human_printer_after.speaker: printer
human_printer_after.text: (laughing) BANDAR KENCANA. Bold type. Front page. I'm never forgetting it again.

human_trader_after.speaker: trader
human_trader_after.text: Bandar Kencana! Thirty years. Ha! Thirty-one, actually.

sign_blank.speaker: narrator
sign_blank.text: The wharf sign reads: BANDAR ______. The paint isn't faded. The letters are just... gone.

sign_restored.speaker: narrator
sign_restored.text: The wharf sign reads: BANDAR KENCANA. The letters look a little smug about it.

bk01_no_crack.speaker: lumi
bk01_no_crack.text: The air at the end of the wharf feels thin. Like a page about to tear. Not yet, though.

human_repairman.speaker: repairman
human_repairman.text: (to his soldering iron) That old set on the top shelf talks to itself. Valves are finished. I keep meaning to throw it out.

C3_02_radio.speaker: narrator
C3_02_radio.text: A big old valve radio on the top shelf. The dial glows faintly.

C3_02_radio.speaker: elias
C3_02_radio.text: (through the speaker) ...oh! Oh, somebody can HEAR me! Spirits! Hello!

C3_02_radio.speaker: elias
C3_02_radio.text: I'm not the radio. I'm IN the radio. Elias. My valve cracked and I can't get out. I've been stuck on the shipping forecast for a month.

C3_02_radio.speaker: lumi
C3_02_radio.text: Where can we find a valve?

C3_02_radio.speaker: elias
C3_02_radio.text: The photo studio across the wharf keeps spares for their flash units. Bottom drawer of the big desk. Please hurry. It's very windy in Dogger.

find_valve.speaker: narrator
find_valve.text: The bottom drawer of the photographer's desk: flash bulbs, film... and a spare glass valve.

drawer_idle.speaker: narrator
drawer_idle.text: Drawers full of film and flash bulbs.

C3_02_elias.speaker: narrator
C3_02_elias.text: Reno climbs the shelf and swaps the cracked valve for the new one. The radio hums, warms, glows...

C3_02_elias.speaker: narrator
C3_02_elias.text: ...and a lanky spirit with an aerial for a cowlick pops out of the speaker grille.

C3_02_elias.speaker: elias
C3_02_elias.text: FREE! Thank you! Elias, Wayfarer, radio spirit, at your service. Mind the cord.

C3_02_elias.speaker: reno
C3_02_elias.text: Reno! That's Lumi! We're looking for whoever's stealing names!

C3_02_elias.speaker: elias
C3_02_elias.text: Stealing... that's why I can't remember this town's name. Nobody can. I tried every station.

C3_02_elias.speaker: elias
C3_02_elias.text: I can tune things. Radios, masts, old broadcasts. If this town ever said its name out loud, the air still remembers it.

C3_02_elias.speaker: narrator
C3_02_elias.text: Elias joined the party! He rides in Reno's satchel. In battle: Spark Coil and Static Burst. In the field: Tune, at radio masts.

C3_02_elias.speaker: elias
C3_02_elias.text: Start with the photo studio. Photographs remember things people forget.

radio_empty.speaker: narrator
radio_empty.text: The old radio plays a quiet song now. The shipping forecast is over.

human_photographer.speaker: photographer
human_photographer.text: (dusting frames) Thirty years of photographs of this town and every caption's gone blank. My handwriting, gone.

human_photographer_after.speaker: photographer
human_photographer_after.text: (writing captions, humming) Bandar Kencana, 1938. Bandar Kencana, 1946. Bandar Kencana, Bandar Kencana...

photo_later.speaker: narrator
photo_later.text: Three faded photographs with blank captions.

photo_look.speaker: narrator
photo_look.text: A faded photograph with a blank caption.

photo_look.speaker: elias
photo_look.text: Lumi's Memory Touch could tell us what it was.

photo_look.speaker: narrator
photo_look.text: (Swap to Lumi with C, then look again.)

photo_done.speaker: narrator
photo_done.text: The caption is written in again, in neat handwriting.

photo_1_touch.speaker: narrator
photo_1_touch.text: Lumi touches the photograph. Firecrackers, red paper, a crowd on the wharf, and a banner going up over the street.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Lumi writes "Wharf, New Year, 1938" on the caption. It stays.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Lumi writes it, and the words slide off the paper.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: Not that one.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Lumi writes it, and the words slide off the paper.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: Not that one.

photo_2_touch.speaker: narrator
photo_2_touch.text: Lumi touches the photograph. Rain hammering the street, sandbags, the printer's apprentices carrying paper up to the first floor.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Lumi writes it, and the words slide off the paper.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: Not that one.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Lumi writes "The big flood, 1926" on the caption. It stays.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Lumi writes it, and the words slide off the paper.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: Not that one.

photo_3_touch.speaker: narrator
photo_3_touch.text: Lumi touches the photograph. A brand-new printing press being winched off a barge, everybody cheering, a dog barking.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Lumi writes it, and the words slide off the paper.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: Not that one.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Lumi writes it, and the words slide off the paper.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: Not that one.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Lumi writes "The new press arrives, 1946" on the caption. It stays.

photos_check.speaker: photographer
photos_check.text: (suddenly) Kencana. Bandar Kencana! How did I forget?

photos_check.speaker: elias
photos_check.text: It's coming back for the humans. But the spirit side is still blank. Feel that? Something tore at the west end of the wharf.

C3_04_veil.speaker: narrator
C3_04_veil.text: Kencana-in-the-Veil: the town's spirit twin, violet and quiet. Spirits wander the street looking at their own hands.

C3_04_veil.speaker: nameless_spirit
C3_04_veil.text: Excuse me. Do you know who I am? I'm the one who... sells the... the paper things?

C3_04_veil.speaker: elias
C3_04_veil.text: Three radio masts. If the town ever broadcast its name, I can tune it back in.

C3_04_veil.speaker: narrator
C3_04_veil.text: New goal: read each mast's plaque, and let Elias Tune the right frequency.

nameless_a.speaker: nameless_spirit
nameless_a.text: I had a name. It was short. Or long. It had a nice sound.

nameless_b.speaker: nameless_spirit
nameless_b.text: The Hall of Records is shut. Something in there keeps saying "tidy, tidy".

nameless_after.speaker: nameless_spirit
nameless_after.text: Kertas-Kecil! That's me! Of the Kencana Paper Kin! Thank you!

kertas_stall.speaker: mak_kertas
kertas_stall.text: I remember my stall even if I can't remember my street. Buy something, dear.

mast_1.speaker: narrator
mast_1.text: Plaque: "Wharf Station. First broadcast at dawn, when the tide was lowest."

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Elias tunes the mast. Static, a whistle... then a voice, decades old:

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: ...good morning from the wharf at Bandar KEN...!

then.speaker: elias
then.text: "KEN"! That's part of it!

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Just static, and somebody's cooking programme.

then.speaker: elias
then.text: Wrong band. Let's read the plaque again.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Just static, and somebody's cooking programme.

then.speaker: elias
then.text: Wrong band. Let's read the plaque again.

mast_2.speaker: narrator
mast_2.text: Plaque: "Market Station. Our signal is neither high nor low, like a fair price."

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Just static, and somebody's cooking programme.

then.speaker: elias
then.text: Wrong band. Let's read the plaque again.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Elias tunes the mast. Static, a whistle... then a voice, decades old:

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: ...prices today in the market of Bandar Ken-CA...!

then.speaker: elias
then.text: "CA"! That's part of it!

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Just static, and somebody's cooking programme.

then.speaker: elias
then.text: Wrong band. Let's read the plaque again.

mast_3.speaker: narrator
mast_3.text: Plaque: "Hill Station. Highest mast in town. Our voice carries furthest."

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Just static, and somebody's cooking programme.

then.speaker: elias
then.text: Wrong band. Let's read the plaque again.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Just static, and somebody's cooking programme.

then.speaker: elias
then.text: Wrong band. Let's read the plaque again.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Elias tunes the mast. Static, a whistle... then a voice, decades old:

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: ...and goodnight from Bandar Kenca-NA...!

then.speaker: elias
then.text: "NA"! That's part of it!

mast_done.speaker: narrator
mast_done.text: The mast hums quietly, still holding its old broadcast.

masts_check.speaker: reno
masts_check.text: KEN, CA, NA! Kencana! Bandar Kencana!

masts_check.speaker: narrator
masts_check.text: Far up the street, the doors of the Hall of Records swing open.

bk04_hall_locked.speaker: narrator
bk04_hall_locked.text: The Hall of Records is shut tight. Inside, a dry voice says "tidy... tidy..."

bk04_hall_locked.speaker: elias
bk04_hall_locked.text: We need the name first. The masts.

bk04_blots_beaten.speaker: reno
bk04_blots_beaten.text: Ugh. My hands are all inky.

bk04_beetle_beaten.speaker: elias
bk04_beetle_beaten.text: A typeset beetle. Somebody's been printing nothing at all.

bk04_mixed_beaten.speaker: lumi
bk04_mixed_beaten.text: They're guarding the masts. Somebody didn't want the name back.

C3_06_clerk_intro.speaker: narrator
C3_06_clerk_intro.text: In the Hall of Records, a tall spirit made of white paper and black ink is wiping a ledger clean, page after page.

C3_06_clerk_intro.speaker: blank_clerk
C3_06_clerk_intro.text: Visitors. Untidy. Names are untidy. They smudge. They tear. They hurt when they're lost.

C3_06_clerk_intro.speaker: lumi
C3_06_clerk_intro.text: Who told you to do this?

C3_06_clerk_intro.speaker: blank_clerk
C3_06_clerk_intro.text: Someone with ink on their fingers. Someone who was very, very sad. Blank is tidy. Blank is SAFE.

C3_06_clerk_outro.speaker: narrator
C3_06_clerk_outro.text: The Blank Clerk crumples like a dropped page. Its ink runs out of it and soaks into the floorboards.

C3_06_clerk_outro.speaker: blank_clerk
C3_06_clerk_outro.text: ...it was so quiet. Nobody could lose anything...

C3_06_clerk_outro.speaker: narrator
C3_06_clerk_outro.text: The ledger falls open. Every page blank, except the stamp inside the cover: a rubber leaf.

C3_06_clerk_outro.speaker: elias
C3_06_clerk_outro.text: "Bukit Getah Estate." That's a rubber estate, up the hill road.

C3_06_clerk_outro.speaker: narrator
C3_06_clerk_outro.text: Got the Clerk's Ledger and the Crystal Earpiece (Elias: RES +3, SPD +2).

C3_07_name_back.speaker: narrator
C3_07_name_back.text: Back at the wharf, the letters climb back onto every sign: BANDAR KENCANA.

C3_07_name_back.speaker: printer
C3_07_name_back.text: (laughing at himself) Bandar Kencana! Bandar Um. Oh dear.

C3_07_name_back.speaker: elias
C3_07_name_back.text: The name's back. For the humans and the spirits.

C3_07_name_back.speaker: lumi
C3_07_name_back.text: Whoever did this sent the Clerk from a rubber estate.

C3_07_name_back.speaker: reno
C3_07_name_back.text: Rubber trees! Do they have trains?

C3_07_name_back.speaker: elias
C3_07_name_back.text: They have a lorry. I know the radio in its cab. Lovely voice. Terrible taste in music.

C3_07_name_back.speaker: lumi
C3_07_name_back.text: Elias... are you coming with us?

C3_07_name_back.speaker: elias
C3_07_name_back.text: Somebody has to tune things for you. Besides, my shelf was getting dusty.
